With so many FMV dating sims out there, most rest somewhere in the middle of the pack: good but not memorable. Cue to Fall in Love with You (aka 恋爱吗？我家猫会后空翻 aka Is It Love? My Cat Can Do Backflips) is another one of these. It offers excellent value, a strong cast, and the characters are fine, but it’s rough around the edges and nothing special.

As college student Ren Jie, you are run over by a scooter and this somehow awakens an AI love assistant named YOYO. This AI occasionally provides unimpressive dating advice and conjures gifts from another dimension, but how it all works is never adequately explained. Although curious about love, the assistant does not raise any interesting topics and her role is inferior to Zero from the Unemployed game. YOYO is a fully AI generated character (possibly the first in the genre) designed to look like a person, so there is uncanny valley whenever she appears.

The six primary love interests are played by real human actors and the cast is strong. Genre veterans, Lei Xiaomi and Wang Nannan, play Lin Wenxi and Xia Wanxing respectively. Wenxi is a kind doctor that channels the teacher from Hello Love: 18 Again. Wanxing is a starlet and childhood friend with some nice flashback scenes. Both know how to work the screen and are consistent. Lesser known actresses play the other roles but they do a good job. Shen Yufei is a sultry reporter with high sex appeal. Gu Panpan is a tomboy who likes to beat you up. Lu Xiaoyu is a younger friend who has a big crush, but thankfully she is not excessively immature. And Suzuki Rei is the softly spoken exchange student who becomes your roommate. 

It’s the personalities and adequate back stories that ensure these six are not one-dimensional. Romance is fairly low-key and tempered, for a slow burn, even though Yufei can be aggressively affectionate. Each character has 3+ endings, based mostly on conversations from chapter 5 and 6, although putting this dialogue together may have worked better. There are early endings too, ala I’ve Fallen For You, but the finales are too short generally. While having 6+ love interests is often problematic, the 5.1 hour runtime and minimal story gives them all enough screen time.

The game is rough around the edges. Scene cuts are quite jarring and frequent. The story flow and pacing could be better. Audio is live recorded (great) but the volume levels needed adjustment. Video quality is inadequate during high motion. Translation seems to be LLM without edits, so there are many pronoun issues and name changes. One nice thing is that skipping through scenes is instantaneous, which helps when re-exploring the nicely branching timeline—it will take 10.5 hours to see everything. Cue to Fall in Love with You is nothing exceptional, but it is a pretty good effort that most genre fans should enjoy.

To me, 恋爱吗？我家猫会后空翻 is a light, cozy FMV romance, and I think people who love cats will enjoy it the most. The game has several cute cat moments, and a few characters even have cat-themed makeup that adds a fun little charm to their scenes. It’s the kind of story that doesn’t aim for big drama, just something soft and warm to relax with.

One thing I genuinely liked is how the endings are distributed. Most characters have at least three different outcomes, and even Yoyo, who is an AI, still gets two endings along with enough unique scenes to feel complete. Because of that, replaying actually feels meaningful instead of repetitive.

The pacing, though, can be a mixed experience. I know many players will appreciate the longer chapters because they allow more time for character interactions. Personally, one chapter felt a bit too long for my taste, and it slowed down the flow more than I expected.

The acting is solid across the board. Nothing overly dramatic, but natural enough that it keeps the story believable and easy to follow. The whole game carries a soft, pleasant vibe, making it a comfortable pick if you want something simple and heartfelt.

Gameplay-wise, it stays on the lighter side, mostly driven by choices. Some routes don’t diverge as strongly as you might hope. A few assets show the AI-assisted elements the developers mentioned, but they don’t really get in the way of the experience.

And honestly, considering the price, this is still a very reasonable choice. You get a decent amount of content, multiple endings, and a cozy atmosphere that’s easy to enjoy without feeling like you're overpaying.

In the end, 恋爱吗？我家猫会后空翻 is the kind of FMV you play more for the mood than for complexity. If you love cats, gentle romances, and small decisions that quietly shape the story, it’s a warm, pleasant experience that feels worth your time.

恋爱吗？我家猫会后空翻, developed and published by 光循花火工作室, is a romance-focused interactive story that blends elements of visual novels, dating simulations, and cinematic presentation into a single experience centered on emotional choices rather than mechanical gameplay. From the opening moments, the game establishes itself as a character-driven narrative where the protagonist, an otherwise ordinary university student, suddenly finds his life transformed after awakening a mysterious “romance system.” This premise sets the tone for a narrative that mixes humor, fantasy, youthful drama, and genuine emotional storytelling, inviting players into a world where everyday encounters gradually unfold into deeper relationships.

At its core, the game is built around branching storylines shaped by the player’s decisions. You interact with six different female leads, each written with a distinct personality, background, and emotional trajectory. Some characters embody gentle warmth, others carry a more lively or rebellious charm, and a few reveal subtle layers through personal conflicts and insecurities. These differences give each romance route its own identity, making replays feel like unique journeys rather than simple variations. The writing emphasizes both playful moments and more heartfelt scenes, and the emotional pacing often shifts from lighthearted banter to introspective conversations about goals, fears, or unspoken feelings. Because choices directly affect character responses and narrative direction, players are encouraged to approach each relationship thoughtfully, aware that even small decisions can alter the tone or outcome of a route.

Visually, the game presents itself with a clean, polished aesthetic that complements its romantic themes. The interface is simple and intuitive, embracing the style of modern visual novels with crisp character art, expressive facial animations, and cinematic framing during key scenes. The developers include multilingual support and full voice acting, allowing each heroine to express personality and emotion through tone and performance rather than just text. This audio-visual pairing enhances immersion, especially during pivotal emotional moments or romantic climaxes where the characters’ voices carry much of the scene’s impact. With multiple languages supported, the game successfully extends its appeal beyond its home audience and offers an accessible entry point for global players interested in narrative-driven romance titles.

Mechanically, the gameplay remains intentionally minimalistic to highlight the storytelling. Most actions revolve around reading dialogue, selecting choices, and watching events unfold through interactive scenes. Because of this, the experience prioritizes narrative immersion over interactivity. There are no mini-games, complex progression systems, or strategic layers to manage. Instead, the pacing closely mirrors that of a cinematic experience: the player advances through conversations, character interactions, and lightly branching pathways that steer the emotional direction of the story. While this approach offers clarity and accessibility, it also means that the game relies heavily on the strength of its writing and characters to maintain player engagement throughout.

One of the game’s strengths lies in the emotional range of its storytelling. Although the premise includes comedic elements—especially the playful exaggeration implied by the title—the narrative does not shy away from more serious themes. Characters struggle with personal dilemmas, wounds from their past, and romantic uncertainties. Moments of vulnerability stand in contrast to the game’s cheerful sections, giving the overall journey more narrative depth than its light premise may initially suggest. For players who enjoy romance routes that blend sweetness with emotional stakes, this balance offers a satisfying sense of progression as relationships evolve naturally rather than through simple tropes.

However, the game’s structure also introduces certain limitations. Because the mechanics remain centered almost exclusively on dialogue choices, players seeking more varied gameplay may find the experience repetitive. Even with multiple routes, the underlying loop is largely the same across playthroughs—click through scenes, choose responses, unlock emotional developments, and progress toward one of the possible endings. The fantasy-like premise of suddenly becoming the romantic focus of multiple characters may also feel exaggerated or unrealistic to players who prefer grounded storytelling. Additionally, the story’s reliance on familiar dating-sim archetypes means that some routes may feel predictable, especially for genre veterans who recognize these character types from similar titles.

Despite its simplicity, the game succeeds when viewed as a romance narrative designed to create emotional engagement rather than challenge or complex interactivity. The polished presentation, diverse cast, full voice acting, and accessible design come together to deliver a modern, easy-to-enjoy romantic experience that caters to players who value story and relationships above all else. Its charm lies in how it blends fantasy wish-fulfillment with genuine emotion, offering multiple romantic paths to explore and characters who encourage repeated playthroughs. For fans of romance visual novels and narrative-driven love stories, 恋爱吗？我家猫会后空翻 provides a warm and engaging journey filled with connection, humor, and heartfelt moments.

This game requires an internet connection (it has online verification – 3rd-party DRM) and has no cloud saves. If your internet connection is lost, your game progress will be lost. Your save file also seems to sync to the developer’s server, not Steam. If the developer’s server is no longer available or cannot be reached, the game becomes unplayable.

I keep FMV games that have no online verification and can be played offline, and I refund FMV games that have online verification. You can’t keep games with online verification because the server will not stay online forever—in other words, it feels more like renting than purchasing.
